entities.paper: Mapping Languages and Demographics with Georeferenced Corpora

twitter_fewer_missing_languages.text: The authors report that, where ground-truth language-use data is available, Twitter has fewer missing languages (cases where census languages are not found in digital texts).

twitter_more_false_positives.text: The authors note that false positives are uncommon overall but occur more in Twitter data, meaning Twitter suggests languages are frequently used in a country when census data does not.

twitter_represents_wealthier_populations.text: The authors imply that Twitter as a platform represents more wealthy populations than general web-crawled data, based on Twitter matching populations better when weighted by GDP and worse when weighted by internet-usage statistics.

urban_collection_alternative.text: The authors offer an alternate interpretation that their Twitter collection is based on urban areas, which tend to have more wealthy populations.

twitter_better_north_america_oceania.text: The authors find that Twitter provides a better representation of North America and Oceania, while the two corpora agree in Europe, parts of Africa with ground-truth data, and South America.

english_spanish_common_on_twitter.text: The authors note that English and Spanish are very common on Twitter, so any country predominantly using these two languages will have a good representation by default.

few_languages_disguise_tpr.text: The authors state that many countries have only a few languages, so a high true positive rate for a country could reflect only one or two languages.

twitter_false_positives_regions.text: The authors report that on Twitter most false positives are in Russia and Eastern Europe, with over-predicted languages also in the US and Canada, South Africa, France, India, and Australia.

false_positive_sources_unresolved.text: The authors state that more research is needed to distinguish between immigration, tourism, and business as alternate sources of false positive languages appearing in digital data sets.

datasets_diverge_different_places.text: The authors say patterns from Twitter and web-crawled data diverge significantly and that this simply reflects that data drawn from Twitter and web pages will likely represent people from different places.

twitter_better_language_inventory.text: 论文指出，Twitter 数据对各国家所使用语言清单的预测优于网络抓取数据。

fewer_missing_languages.text: 在存在真实语言使用数据的国家中，仍有一些国家这些语料未涵盖当地人口产生的全部语言，即并非所有普查中的语言都能在数字文本中找到；在这种情况下，Twitter 缺失的语言更少。

better_north_america_oceania.text: 两种语料在很多情况下对各国语言预测一致（欧洲、有真实数据的部分非洲地区、南美洲），但 Twitter 对北美和大洋洲提供了更好的代表性。

evaluation_method_tpr_fpr.text: 论文用真阳性率（普查语言中被文本数据找到的比例）和假阳性率（文本数据声称使用但普查中没有的语言）比较语料与底层人口，并采用“某语言占该国语料至少5%即视为使用”的阈值来评估，而不要求精确预测各语言使用者比例。

twitter_fewer_false_positives_caveat.text: 在一般意义上，这些语料很少预测实际不存在的语言使用；但 Twitter 数据中的假阳性更多（虽不常见），且在特定地区如美国和加拿大、南非、法国、印度、澳大利亚存在过度预测语言的情况。

corpus_population_correlation.text: 论文发现两种数据集代表非常不同的人口，并与实际人口相关：社交媒体（Twitter）r=0.60，网络抓取 r=0.49。

ground_truth_sources.text: 语言使用的真实基准采用联合国国家级普查汇总数据，在不可用时回退到 CIA World Factbook 数据；语言使用真实数据比人口数据稀疏得多，例如联合国语言数据集中没有巴西的信息。

twitter_wealthier_populations.text: 论文观察到 Twitter 数据在按 GDP 加权人口时匹配更好、按互联网使用统计加权时更差，这暗示 Twitter 平台比一般网络抓取数据代表更富裕的人群，也可能是其采集基于城市地区所致。
